answer: Allocate agent grants per verified human controller. A registrar checks enrollment against existing people and issues one anonymous credential. Each claim reveals a nullifier bound to the grant program and period; the ledger accepts it once, regardless of the agent key. A controller's lotus classifier, umber color matcher, and echo analyzer therefore share one grant. To farm more grants, an attacker must recruit and compensate additional people. This requires reliable duplicate detection, registrar integrity, and resistance to credential theft.
